query: For AlCrFeNiSi powder feedstock intended for additively manufactured miniature components, what single intervention could overcome the residual thermal stresses, degraded mechanical properties, and processing complexity associated with mainstream metallic additive-manufacturing regimes? Formulate one hypothesis that specifies the intervention and mechanism, predicts outcomes relative to components made under conventional high-thermal-load additive-manufacturing conditions, states the applicable processing window, geometry, and test conditions, identifies supporting prior evidence, and describes a falsification experiment.

generation.hypothesis: Depositing AlCrFeNiSi feedstock by high-velocity cold-spray additive manufacturing (CSAM) at gas temperatures ≤500 °C will eliminate most solidification-induced residual thermal stress and refine the microstructure through impact-driven severe plastic deformation, thereby producing miniature components whose tensile yield strength and uniform elongation are each ≥10 % higher than counterparts produced by conventional laser powder-bed fusion (LPBF) under otherwise identical geometries.
generation.material_initial_state: Pre-alloyed argon-atomised AlCrFeNiSi powder with D50 ≈ 20 µm, spherical morphology, stored dry at 25 °C.
generation.intervention: Replace melt-based LPBF with solid-state high-velocity cold-spray deposition using N2 or He propellant at 20–30 bar and 400–500 °C nozzle exit temperature, followed by a single low-temperature (550 °C, 1 h) stress-relief anneal in Ar.
generation.conditions: Deposition on 316L stainless steel substrates held below 200 °C; layer thickness 30–50 µm; build height ≤5 mm; coupon geometry: ASTM E8 miniature dog-bones, gauge 10 mm × 2 mm × 1 mm; post-deposition anneal as above; room-temperature mechanical testing at 10-3 s−1 strain rate.
generation.structural_mediator: Ultrafine (≤300 nm) equiaxed grains formed by adiabatic shear-induced dynamic recrystallisation and high dislocation density retained after low-T anneal; absence of columnar solidification cells and shrinkage porosity.
generation.mechanism: Because CSAM keeps particle temperature below the solidus, rapid plastic deformation upon impact bonds particles in the solid state, avoiding melt pool solidification and its associated thermal gradients. The severe plastic deformation drives dynamic recrystallisation that refines grains and stores compressive residual stresses that counteract tensile stresses. The subsequent low-T anneal partially relieves dislocations while preserving grain refinement, enhancing both strength (Hall–Petch) and ductility (reduced stress concentrators).
generation.predicted_outcome: Relative to LPBF-fabricated AlCrFeNiSi coupons: (1) X-ray diffraction or hole-drilling shows ≥80 % lower net tensile residual stress (≤50 MPa versus ≥250 MPa); (2) tensile yield strength increases by 10–20 %; (3) uniform elongation increases by ≥10 % absolute (e.g., from 8 % to ≥18 %); (4) fracture surfaces show ductile microvoid coalescence rather than hot-tearing facets.
generation.baseline: AlCrFeNiSi miniature coupons built by state-of-practice LPBF (200 W fibre laser, 80 µm hatch, 60 µm layer, 30–50 µs exposure) followed by standard 1 h/550 °C stress-relief.
generation.boundary: Valid for wall or lattice struts <3 mm thick; gas temperature must stay below solidus (~650 °C) to prevent partial melting; annealing above 600 °C or for >2 h may over-coarsen grains and negate benefits.
generation.uncertainty: Limited published data on CSAM of high-entropy alloys; potential issues with retained porosity and anisotropy remain unquantified; quantitative improvement margins may vary ±5 %.

falsification_experiment.design: Produce two sets (n=5 each) of miniature AlCrFeNiSi dog-bone specimens: Set A by LPBF (baseline) and Set B by CSAM+anneal (intervention). Characterise residual stresses via sin2ψ XRD and incremental hole-drilling, measure density (Archimedes), image microstructure (EBSD, TEM), and conduct quasi-static tensile tests.
measurements: Residual stress magnitude and sign in gauge section
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: The hypothesis is falsified if ANY of the following hold for Set B relative to Set A: (i) residual tensile stress is reduced by <50 %; OR (ii) yield strength increase <10 %; OR (iii) uniform elongation increase <10 % absolute; OR (iv) grain size is not finer (<500 nm).
